meaning_or_distinction: gives the reason as the information-bearing cause
confusables: because of + NP; since + finite clause
evidence_note: Core causal subordinator; use when the answer to why is foregrounded.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CAUSE-BECAUSE-VS-BECAUSE-OF.

target_pattern: main clause + because of + noun or V-ing
meaning_or_distinction: gives a cause with a non-clausal complement
confusables: because + finite clause; due to + NP
evidence_note: The complement-form contrast is high-frequency and atomically testable.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CAUSE-BECAUSE-OF.

target_pattern: Since + finite clause / since + time point
meaning_or_distinction: introduces a background reason before a finite clause or marks the starting point of a continuing period
evidence_note: Completed recognition distinguishes causal since from temporal since.

meaning_or_distinction: introduces a background reason, often in written explanation
evidence_note: Completed recognition owns only background-reason as; LINK-041 owns temporal as.

target_pattern: result or situation + due to + noun or V-ing
meaning_or_distinction: gives a neutral-to-formal cause phrase
confusables: because of + NP; owing to + NP
evidence_note: Modern use is broader than predicative-only rules claim.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CAUSE-DUE-TO.

target_pattern: main clause + owing to + noun or V-ing
meaning_or_distinction: gives a formal cause phrase
confusables: because of + NP; due to + NP
evidence_note: Recognition and formal-writing item, not a correction of because of.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CAUSE-OWING-TO.

target_pattern: main clause + thanks to + noun or V-ing
meaning_or_distinction: attributes a result to a cause, sometimes ironically
confusables: because of + NP; due to + NP
evidence_note: Do not claim that the result must be favorable.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CAUSE-THANKS-TO.

target_pattern: main clause + for lack of + needed resource
meaning_or_distinction: attributes an outcome to an absent needed resource or quality
confusables: because of a lack of + NP; without + NP
evidence_note: Productive with evidence, time, resources, and interest.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CAUSE-FOR-LACK-OF.

target_pattern: decision or assessment + in light of + fact
meaning_or_distinction: frames a decision as responsive to relevant information
confusables: because of + NP; in view of + NP
evidence_note: Use evidence or changed circumstances, not a simple physical cause.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CAUSE-IN-LIGHT-OF.

meaning_or_distinction: marks a logical result across two independent clauses
evidence_note: Teach sentence punctuation and position; not comma-splice punctuation.

anchor: as a result as a sentence connector
target_pattern: independent clause. As a result, independent clause
meaning_or_distinction: marks a result of the preceding statement
confusables: as a result of + NP; therefore
evidence_note: Separate connector from prepositional as a result of.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CAUSE-AS-A-RESULT-OF.

meaning_or_distinction: marks a formal logical consequence
evidence_note: Keep as recognition/formal writing, not a required synonym drill.

meaning_or_distinction: states a contrary fact without preventing the main result
confusables: despite + NP;though + finite clause;even though + finite clause;while + finite clause
evidence_note: Completed core-pattern recognition preserves ordinary finite-clause alternatives.

meaning_or_distinction: states concession in a more conversational alternative to although
confusables: although + finite clause; even though + finite clause
evidence_note: Use an ordinary clause-initial or medial example.

meaning_or_distinction: adds a brief afterthought concession after a statement
evidence_note: Do not present sentence-final though as equivalent in all formal writing.

target_pattern: Even though + fact / Even if + hypothetical case
meaning_or_distinction: distinguishes emphatic factual concession from a hypothetical condition whose occurrence does not change the result
evidence_note: Merged LINK-016 and LINK-031; one card owns the factual-versus-hypothetical even contrast.

anchor: despite or in spite of + NP or V-ing
target_pattern: Despite or In spite of + noun or V-ing, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: states concession before a non-finite complement
evidence_note: Do not create a false preference between despite and in spite of.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CONCESSION-IN-SPITE-OF and AR-CONCESSION-DESPITE.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced concessive clause when its understood subject matches the main-clause subject
evidence_note: Reduction requires recoverable shared subject.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a passive reduced concessive clause with a recoverable subject
evidence_note: Use cases such as Although approved, the plan was delayed.

meaning_or_distinction: uses an adjective reduction after although
confusables: although + subject + be + adjective; despite + NP
evidence_note: The omitted subject and be verb must be clear from context.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a prepositional reduction after although
evidence_note: Use stable idiomatic forms such as although in doubt.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a predicative nominal reduction after although
evidence_note: Use roles or states such as although a student, she worked full-time.

meaning_or_distinction: allows several licensed reduced concession shapes with a main-clause-controlled understood subject
evidence_note: Non-atomic overview replaced by shape-specific items
notes: Active homes are LINK-THOUGH-VING, LINK-THOUGH-PAST-PART, LINK-THOUGH-ADJP, LINK-THOUGH-PP, and LINK-THOUGH-PRED-NP.

anchor: although with an explicit subject after a reduction
target_pattern: Although + subject + be + complement, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: keeps the finite clause when the reduced form would create an unclear or mismatched subject
evidence_note: Negative boundary: do not reduce across a subject mismatch.

meaning_or_distinction: contrasts two facts or locates simultaneous actions; context determines the reading
evidence_note: Completed recognition owns the contrast-versus-simultaneity boundary.

meaning_or_distinction: sets a formal contrast between facts, groups, or policies
evidence_note: Prefer analytic or policy contexts.

target_pattern: main clause + regardless of whether + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: states that an outcome is unaffected by either possibility
confusables: even if + finite clause; despite + NP
evidence_note: The whether clause is the complement of of, not a bare finite clause.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CONCESSION-REGARDLESS-OF.

target_pattern: main clause + in the face of + challenge or evidence
meaning_or_distinction: states persistence despite genuine adversity or contrary evidence
confusables: despite + NP; when faced with + NP
evidence_note: Avoid treating it as a neutral synonym in trivial contexts.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CONCESSION-IN-THE-FACE-OF.

meaning_or_distinction: states an open or real condition without presenting the event as expected
confusables: unless + finite clause;in case + finite clause;when + finite clause
evidence_note: Core conditional linker; completed contrast note distinguishes uncertain if from expected when.

meaning_or_distinction: means if the stated condition does not happen
confusables: if not + finite clause; except if
evidence_note: Do not use unless where the intended condition is affirmative.

target_pattern: Even if + subject + verb, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: states that the result holds in a hypothetical case
confusables: even though + finite clause;regardless of whether
evidence_note: Merged into LINK-016
notes: Reciprocal duplicate; LINK-016 owns factual even though versus hypothetical even if.

anchor: as long as or so long as + finite clause
target_pattern: main clause + as/so long as + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: states a necessary condition or permitted limit; so long as is a little more informal
evidence_note: Completed variant recognition; use condition contexts, not duration contexts.

anchor: provided or providing that + finite clause
target_pattern: Provided or Providing + subject + verb, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: states a formal or contract-like condition
confusables: if + finite clause; as long as + finite clause
evidence_note: Both forms occur; do not make a blank that rejects the other.

target_pattern: main clause + in case + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: states a precaution against a possible event
confusables: if + finite clause; in case of + NP
evidence_note: Precaution, not a prediction that the event will occur.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CONDITION-IN-CASE-OF boundary.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced condition with omitted subject and be
confusables: if + finite clause; unless + finite clause
evidence_note: Use fixed productive forms such as if necessary or if possible.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced condition with omitted subject and be
evidence_note: Use clear shared-subject contexts such as if in doubt.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a passive reduced condition
confusables: if + finite passive clause; unless + past participle clause
evidence_note: Use recoverable passive subjects, e.g. If approved, the request will proceed.

target_pattern: Unless otherwise stated / Unless stated otherwise
meaning_or_distinction: uses a conventional passive exception formula meaning unless another rule or instruction says otherwise
confusables: unless + finite clause;if not + finite clause
evidence_note: Do not apply an ordinary shared-affected-subject analysis to the following main-clause noun.

meaning_or_distinction: locates the main event at the time of another event
confusables: while + finite clause; once + finite clause
evidence_note: Core temporal linker.

meaning_or_distinction: locates two actions as simultaneous over a period
confusables: when + finite clause; while + contrast clause
evidence_note: Contrast duration/simultaneity with single time-point when.

meaning_or_distinction: marks two actions developing or happening together
confusables: when + finite clause; because + finite clause
evidence_note: Context must block causal reading.

meaning_or_distinction: orders one full event earlier than another
evidence_note: Finite alternative has its own expressed subject.

meaning_or_distinction: orders the main event later than another full event
evidence_note: Finite alternative has its own expressed subject.

target_pattern: Before or After + V-ing, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: uses a non-finite time clause with a recoverable shared subject
confusables: before or after + finite clause; V-ing free clause
evidence_note: Do not migrate this linker-headed reduction into free non-finite clauses.
notes: Migrates TRAP-COMPLEMENT-BEFORE-AFTER-VING.

meaning_or_distinction: sets the endpoint up to which a situation continues or waits
evidence_note: Until is the broad neutral default; till is conversational. Keep NP time expressions in the preposition deck.

meaning_or_distinction: states that one event follows as soon as a condition/event is complete
confusables: when + finite clause; after + finite clause
evidence_note: Often implies a threshold or completed trigger.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced passive time/condition clause
confusables: once + finite passive clause; if + past participle clause
evidence_note: Use cases such as Once approved, the change takes effect.

target_pattern: main clause + as soon as + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: marks the earliest time at which the main action follows
confusables: once + finite clause; when + finite clause
evidence_note: Avoid an unsupported reduced as soon as form.

anchor: future time clauses use present forms
connector_or_marker: when; after; before; until; once; as soon as
target_pattern: future main clause + linker + present-tense time clause
meaning_or_distinction: uses present forms in a future time clause rather than will
confusables: will in time clause; if + future condition
evidence_note: Teach a real temporal clause, not a blanket ban on will.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced time clause with a recoverable shared subject
confusables: when + finite clause; free V-ing clause
evidence_note: Do not reduce if the understood subject differs.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a passive reduced time clause
confusables: when + finite passive clause; once + past-participle clause
evidence_note: Use forms such as when completed or when compared with.

target_pattern: When + adjective or prepositional phrase, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced state/time clause
confusables: when + finite clause; if + AdjP or PP
evidence_note: Use conventional contexts such as when ready or when in doubt.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced simultaneous-action clause with a shared subject
confusables: while + finite clause; when + V-ing clause
evidence_note: Not a free participial clause: while remains the linker.

target_pattern: main clause + so that + subject + modal or appropriate finite verb
meaning_or_distinction: states a purpose with an expressed intended actor, modality, or explicitly stated result
evidence_note: Use can, could, may, might, will, would, or a natural finite predicate as context requires; use a distinct subject when contrasting with a shared-subject infinitive.

target_pattern: main clause + in order that + subject + modal or appropriate finite verb
meaning_or_distinction: states purpose in a more formal finite-clause pattern
confusables: so that + finite clause;in order to + infinitive
evidence_note: Use completed formal contexts and acknowledge so that often fits; distinguish the finite clause from in order to + infinitive.

anchor: as if versus informal like + finite clause
target_pattern: main clause + as if/like + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: compares appearance or behavior with an imagined situation; as if is the neutral default and clausal like is common in informal AmE
evidence_note: Register-aware contrast prevents a false ban on informal like + clause; LINK-057 owns as if versus as though.

target_pattern: main clause + as though + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: gives a slightly more formal alternative to as if
confusables: as if + finite clause; like + NP
evidence_note: Do not force a choice where either is natural.

anchor: modal remoteness after as if or as though
target_pattern: main clause + as if or as though + past form
meaning_or_distinction: uses a past form to mark unreal, hypothetical, or distancing comparison rather than necessarily past time
evidence_note: Use an explicitly unreal context for objective retrieval; do not claim every past form after as if is counterfactual.

meaning_or_distinction: coordinates a contrast within one sentence
evidence_note: Teach comma before but when it joins independent clauses.

meaning_or_distinction: connects a contrast across sentences or after a semicolon
evidence_note: Avoid comma-splice treatment of however.

anchor: by contrast or in contrast as a sentence connector
meaning_or_distinction: marks an explicit comparison with a preceding case
confusables: in contrast to/with + NP;whereas + finite clause
evidence_note: Both by contrast and in contrast are established sentence connectors.

anchor: in contrast to or with + NP
target_pattern: In contrast to/with + noun, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: supplies an explicit noun-phrase comparison standard
evidence_note: Form-conversion card distinguishes the sentence connector from the NP-complement frame.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CONTRAST-CONTRARY-TO boundary.

target_pattern: Contrary to + expectation or claim, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: states that reality conflicts with an expectation or statement
confusables: in contrast to + NP; despite + NP
evidence_note: Not interchangeable with in contrast to in every context.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CONTRAST-CONTRARY-TO.

target_pattern: In case of + event or emergency, instruction
meaning_or_distinction: uses a noun-complement contingency phrase
confusables: in case + finite clause; if + finite clause
evidence_note: Included as a boundary contrast because in case + clause is high-value.
notes: Migrates FIXED-CONDITION-IN-CASE-OF.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a bounded formal verbless concession with omitted subject and be
evidence_note: Evidence-qualified replacement for the former blanket exclusion.
notes: Teach only the supported formal AdjP pattern; do not generalize to every reduced complement shape.

target_pattern: by the time + subject + verb, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: sets one event as the reference deadline before or at which another state is already true
evidence_note: Rerouted from PREP-TIME-BY-THE-TIME
notes: Use explicit event-versus-clock-time contexts; tense selection must remain natural.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a formal compact reduced concessive action whose understood subject is the main-clause subject
evidence_note: Shape-specific reduction
notes: The omitted subject must normally be the main-clause subject; otherwise use a finite clause.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a passive reduced concession whose affected understood subject is the main-clause subject
confusables: though + finite passive clause;although + past participle
evidence_note: Shape-specific reduction
notes: Use a bounded example such as Though injured, the athlete finished the race.

meaning_or_distinction: uses an adjective state as a reduced concession with an omitted subject and be
evidence_note: Shape-specific reduction
notes: The adjective must describe the main-clause subject.

meaning_or_distinction: uses an idiomatic prepositional state as a reduced concession
evidence_note: Shape-specific reduction
notes: Use stable bounded forms such as though under pressure, with the state applying to the main-clause subject.

target_pattern: Though + role noun phrase, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: uses a role or status as a reduced concession with omitted subject and be
evidence_note: Shape-specific reduction
notes: Use an article-bearing role whose referent is the main-clause subject.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a passive reduced while-clause whose affected subject is the main-clause subject
confusables: while + finite passive clause;when + past participle
evidence_note: Required reduced-linker grid
notes: Use a bounded context such as While located downtown, the clinic served...

meaning_or_distinction: uses an adjective state as a reduced while-clause with omitted subject and be
evidence_note: Required reduced-linker grid
notes: The adjective must describe the main-clause subject and the context must distinguish time or contrast.

meaning_or_distinction: uses an idiomatic prepositional state as a reduced while-clause
evidence_note: Required reduced-linker grid
notes: Use stable forms such as while in college, with the state applying to the main-clause subject.

target_pattern: While + role noun phrase, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: uses a role or status as a compact reduced while-clause with omitted subject and be
evidence_note: Required reduced-linker grid
notes: The role phrase must refer to the main-clause subject; the finite version is more natural in conversation.

target_pattern: When + role noun phrase, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: uses a compressed formal former-role or life-stage clause with omitted subject and be
evidence_note: C1 reduced time pattern
notes: Use a role whose referent is clearly the main-clause subject; prefer the finite form or as + role NP in ordinary conversation.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a reduced active condition whose understood actor is the main-clause subject
evidence_note: Required reduced-linker grid
notes: Use a bounded conditional context such as If traveling abroad, you...; otherwise retain the finite subject.

target_pattern: If + role noun phrase, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: uses a role or status as a compact reduced condition with omitted subject and be
evidence_note: Required reduced-linker grid
notes: The role phrase describes the main-clause subject; the finite form is usually more natural in conversation.

meaning_or_distinction: identifies which person or thing is meant
evidence_note: Meaning test: removing the clause changes the reference.

meaning_or_distinction: adds extra information about an already identified antecedent
evidence_note: Commas reflect added rather than identifying information.

meaning_or_distinction: uses who when the relative pronoun is the subject of a people-relative
evidence_note: No pronoun omission for a subject relative.

meaning_or_distinction: uses which when the relative pronoun is the subject of a thing-relative
evidence_note: Required subject-relative boundary
notes: Use defining and non-defining contexts separately; zero cannot replace a subject relative marker.

anchor: that as subject in a defining relative
meaning_or_distinction: uses that as the expressed subject marker in a defining people or thing relative
evidence_note: Atomicity fix
notes: Subject-specific item; object that and zero boundaries live in REL-007 through REL-009, and that is unavailable in non-defining relatives.

anchor: who or whom as object relative
target_pattern: person + who or whom + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: uses who in neutral defining relatives and whom chiefly in formal object position
evidence_note: Core people-object relative contrast
notes: Make role observable because another subject follows the pronoun; that and zero are defining-only, and fronted prepositions require whom.

anchor: which or that as object relative
target_pattern: thing + which or that + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: uses which or that for a defining object relative
evidence_note: Do not imply a false universal choice between which and that.

meaning_or_distinction: omits the pronoun in a defining relative when it is the object
evidence_note: The following noun/pronoun must make the clause subject visible.

target_pattern: noun + who or which or that + verb
meaning_or_distinction: retains a subject relative pronoun because omission would remove the clause subject
evidence_note: A clear repair card can contrast The person who called with invalid zero omission.

meaning_or_distinction: marks possession in a relative clause for people and also organizations or things
evidence_note: Avoid the false rule that whose is people-only.

meaning_or_distinction: modifies a place by locating an event or state
confusables: in which + finite clause; when + finite clause
evidence_note: Use a genuine location antecedent.

anchor: in which as formal place relative
meaning_or_distinction: uses fronted preposition plus which in formal writing
evidence_note: A formal alternative, not a repair of where.

target_pattern: time or occasion + when + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: modifies a time by locating an event
confusables: on which + finite clause; where + finite clause
evidence_note: Use a time antecedent, not a reason noun.

anchor: on which as formal time relative
target_pattern: day or date + on which + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: uses fronted preposition plus which in formal writing
confusables: when + finite clause; that + finite clause
evidence_note: Use dates, days, or occasions where the preposition is meaningful.

meaning_or_distinction: modifies reason by giving an explanation
confusables: because + finite clause; reason that + clause
evidence_note: Keep distinct from content noun clauses in module 04.

meaning_or_distinction: uses neutral preposition stranding in a defining object relative
confusables: fronted preposition + whom or which; no preposition
evidence_note: Sentence-final prepositions are grammatical here.
notes: Migrates TRAP-RELATIVE-STRANDED-PREPOSITION.

anchor: fronted preposition plus whom or which
target_pattern: noun + preposition + whom or which + subject + verb
meaning_or_distinction: uses preposition fronting in a formal relative clause
evidence_note: Use whom for people and which for things after the fronted preposition.
notes: Migrates TRAP-RELATIVE-FRONTED-PREPOSITION.

meaning_or_distinction: uses that with a stranded preposition rather than preposition + that
confusables: preposition + that; fronted whom or which
evidence_note: Atomic repair: the alternative is grammatically distinct, not merely more formal.
notes: Migrates TRAP-RELATIVE-NO-PREP-THAT.

anchor: zero object relative with stranded preposition
meaning_or_distinction: allows pronoun omission in a defining object relative with a stranded preposition
evidence_note: Do not omit the pronoun after a fronted preposition.
notes: Migrates TRAP-RELATIVE-OMITTED-PRONOUN.

anchor: no that or zero in non-defining relatives
meaning_or_distinction: keeps who or which because non-defining relatives do not use that or zero
evidence_note: Commas and antecedent reference must be visible in the prompt.

target_pattern: noun, preposition + whom or which + clause,
meaning_or_distinction: uses formal fronting with whom/which or neutral stranding with who/which, but not that or zero, in non-defining clauses
evidence_note: Required placement and relative-type boundary
notes: Use only an unambiguous non-defining antecedent; fronted prepositions require whom/which, while neutral stranding can use who/which.

anchor: quantifier plus of whom or which
target_pattern: noun, quantifier + of whom or which + verb,
meaning_or_distinction: adds a non-defining quantified subset or whole relation
evidence_note: High-value formal pattern such as several of whom.

target_pattern: plural set, all of which + verb
meaning_or_distinction: refers back to all members of a recoverable plural set in a non-defining relative
confusables: all of them;which referring to a proposition
evidence_note: Corrected antecedent scope
notes: Use only a recoverable plural set; REL-041 owns which commenting on a whole proposition.

meaning_or_distinction: attaches the relative clause to the intended noun and rewrites when attachment is ambiguous
evidence_note: Use context/repair rather than a decontextualized grammar label.

meaning_or_distinction: reduces a defining active relative when the noun is the understood subject of the action
confusables: noun + who or which + finite clause; free V-ing clause
evidence_note: Noun-modifying location keeps it in module 06, not module 07.

meaning_or_distinction: reduces a passive relative when the noun receives the action
confusables: noun + that was + past participle; free past-participle clause
evidence_note: Use a clear passive relation such as documents submitted yesterday.

meaning_or_distinction: modifies a noun with an ongoing passive relative
confusables: noun + past participle phrase; finite passive relative
evidence_note: Retain being only when ongoing action matters.

target_pattern: noun + V-ing phrase / noun + who or which + verb
meaning_or_distinction: chooses reduction when it preserves the intended active noun-modifying relation
confusables: free V-ing clause; past-participle reduced relative
evidence_note: Do not reduce where tense, modality, or a distinct subject is necessary.

anchor: past participle versus finite passive relative
target_pattern: noun + past participle phrase / noun + that was + past participle
meaning_or_distinction: chooses a passive reduced relative when no finite tense or modal distinction is needed
confusables: active V-ing reduced relative; free past-participle clause
evidence_note: Do not treat every past participle after a noun as a reduced relative without semantic fit.

anchor: ordinal or superlative noun plus to-infinitive
target_pattern: ordinal or superlative noun + to + verb
meaning_or_distinction: modifies the first, last, next, only, or best noun by a future, intended, or defining action
confusables: noun complement + to-inf; V-ing reduced relative
evidence_note: Includes the first person to arrive.

meaning_or_distinction: uses a to-infinitive to identify the remaining available option
confusables: noun complement + to-inf; the first person to + verb
evidence_note: Required plan boundary example; prompt must make the identifying relation clear.

meaning_or_distinction: modifies an indefinite person or thing by a needed, possible, or intended action
evidence_note: Use forms such as someone to ask or something to eat.

anchor: a noun with a passive-like to-infinitive gap
target_pattern: noun + to + verb + preposition or object gap
meaning_or_distinction: modifies a noun by an action performed to, with, or on it
confusables: passive finite relative; adjective plus infinitive
evidence_note: Use natural examples such as a chair to sit on or work to finish.

meaning_or_distinction: defers ambiguous noun-plus-infinitive patterns when the phrase names content rather than modifies a referential noun
confusables: a decision to leave; the first person to leave
evidence_note: Cross-module boundary already taught
notes: Module 04 teaches noun content complements, while active Module 06 cards teach ordinal and superlative noun modifiers; a single forced contrast would conflate two noun classes.

meaning_or_distinction: is excluded here when that clause supplies the content of a noun rather than modifies an antecedent
evidence_note: Route stable noun content clauses to module 04.
notes: Keep a boundary note only; do not duplicate module 04 cards.

meaning_or_distinction: is excluded here because what introduces a free relative rather than modifying an overt noun
evidence_note: No overt antecedent means it is outside the noun-modifying core.

target_pattern: place + where clause / place + in which clause
meaning_or_distinction: chooses neutral where or formal in which without treating either as erroneous
evidence_note: Use the same place meaning so register is the decision.

anchor: who versus that in defining people relatives
target_pattern: person + who or that + finite clause
meaning_or_distinction: allows both in defining people relatives while preserving who in non-defining clauses
evidence_note: Accepted AmE alternatives
notes: Use a completed acceptance-aware card and Also OK; never force who versus that in a neutral defining blank.

anchor: which versus that in defining thing relatives
target_pattern: thing + which or that + finite clause
meaning_or_distinction: allows both common defining choices with a context-sensitive style note
evidence_note: Accepted defining-relative alternatives
notes: Use a completed acceptance-aware card and Also OK; never claim one is universally wrong.

anchor: comma changes reference in a relative clause
target_pattern: noun comma relative clause / noun relative clause
meaning_or_distinction: uses commas only for added non-defining information
evidence_note: Duplicate decision retired after card-level audit.
notes: Merged into REL-002, which preserves both subset and already-identified-whole readings in one punctuation-and-reference contrast.

anchor: which referring to a preceding clause
meaning_or_distinction: adds a non-defining comment on a whole preceding proposition
confusables: which referring to nearest noun; this fact
evidence_note: Make whole-clause antecedent explicit to avoid attachment ambiguity.

anchor: no that for a whole-clause comment
meaning_or_distinction: uses which, not that, for a non-defining comment on a preceding clause
confusables: that clause; which referring to noun
evidence_note: Keep this narrow: it is a whole-clause non-defining pattern.

target_pattern: thing, the feature of which + verb
meaning_or_distinction: uses a formal alternative to whose for an inanimate possessive relation
evidence_note: Recognition/formal writing item; not a correction of whose.

meaning_or_distinction: uses whom where formal preposition fronting requires an object form
evidence_note: Duplicate decision retired after card-level audit.
notes: Merged into REL-016; REL-017 separately retains the whom-versus-which morphology boundary after a fronted preposition.

target_pattern: V-ing or past-participle clause, main clause
meaning_or_distinction: is excluded here when the non-finite clause modifies the main-clause subject rather than a noun phrase
confusables: noun + reduced relative; free non-finite clause
evidence_note: Route free modifiers to module 07.

anchor: postpositive adjective phrase after an indefinite pronoun
meaning_or_distinction: modifies something, anything, or nothing with an adjective phrase placed after the pronoun

target_pattern: With + noun + past participle, main clause

meaning_or_distinction: adds a state accompanying the main event

anchor: passive free participle requires affected subject

target_pattern: V-ing, matching main clause / finite linker clause

target_pattern: Past participle phrase, affected main subject / finite passive clause

target_pattern: main clause, V-ing phrase / main clause and finite clause
